sources.title: Stillman Drake, Galileo at Work: His Scientific Biography (1978)

curiosity.rationale: On hearing secondhand reports of a Dutch spyglass, built and improved his own within months and immediately turned it skyward rather than only toward the terrestrial/military uses it was marketed for — documented, specific instance.

analytical_rigor.rationale: Inclined-plane and pendulum experiments produced quantitative, repeatable measurements of motion (Drake), a documented quantitative methodology distinct from qualitative Aristotelian physics.

intuitive_synthesis.rationale: Connected independent telescopic observations (Jupiter's moons, Venus's phases) into a single coherent argument for heliocentrism in Sidereus Nuncius and the Dialogue — documented synthesis across separate observational threads.

independent_thinking.rationale: Continued publicly advocating heliocentrism after the Church's explicit 1616 injunction against teaching it, leading directly to his 1633 trial — an extraordinarily well-documented, sustained instance of holding a position against direct authority.

belief_updating.rationale: Documented resistance to Kepler's elliptical-orbit model even after Kepler published supporting evidence, continuing to favor circular orbits — a specific, corroborated instance of not revising a view under new evidence.

creative_originality.rationale: Applying a novel instrument (the improved telescope) systematically to astronomical observation, rather than only the marketed military/nautical use, was a genuinely original methodological move, though it built on an existing invention rather than inventing from nothing.

experimentation.rationale: Inclined-plane experiments measuring falling-body acceleration are specific, documented, and repeated across Drake's reconstruction of his notebooks.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Worked across astronomy, kinematics, and applied instrument-making (the military/geometric compass he sold), a real but more modest range than some peers — moderate band, not extreme.

discipline.rationale: Sustained, systematic nightly observation logs underlying Sidereus Nuncius (1610), published within months of first observing — evidences a disciplined observational routine.

deep_focus.rationale: Same sustained observational campaign; documented but a single (if extended) instance rather than a lifelong pattern verified across multiple independent episodes.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Published the Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems (1632) after an explicit prior warning, with the direct, documented consequence of trial and house arrest — among the best-documented risk-taking instances in the history of science.

persistence.rationale: Continued advocating and publishing heliocentric arguments across decades despite escalating institutional pressure, up to the point of formal trial.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained public disputes with Church authorities and rival astronomers (the Grassi comet dispute, the sunspot-priority dispute with Christoph Scheiner) — documented pattern of engaging rather than avoiding conflict.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Wrote the Dialogue in vernacular Italian rather than scholarly Latin specifically to reach a wider public, and structured it as a pointed rhetorical dialogue including a character widely read as mocking a prior Church-aligned position — a documented, deliberately provocative communication choice.

persuasiveness.rationale: The Dialogue's accessible, dialogue-format structure was a deliberate rhetorical strategy to persuade a lay audience, documented via his own prefatory remarks and its wide contemporary readership.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Continued refining observational technique and instrument quality well beyond what any single publication required, documented across his working notebooks.

competitiveness.rationale: The public priority dispute with Scheiner over sunspot observations, and his rush to publish Sidereus Nuncius before others could claim the same telescopic discoveries, show real priority-consciousness — a moderate, not extreme, documented pattern.

autonomy_need.rationale: Documented letters show him actively petitioning the Medici court for a position specifically to escape university teaching obligations and gain more independent research time.

resourcefulness.rationale: Reconstructed and substantially improved the telescope from only secondhand description of the Dutch design, without access to an actual example — a specific, well-documented instance of resourceful technical improvisation.

opportunity_sensing.rationale: Recognized the telescope's scientific (not just military/nautical) potential immediately on hearing of it secondhand, and acted within months — a clear, documented, fast recognition-and-action instance.

proactive_agency.rationale: Self-initiated the Medici court petition and the rapid telescope-improvement effort without being asked by any patron or institution — documented via his own correspondence.

execution_speed.rationale: Built an improved telescope within months of hearing about the concept and published Sidereus Nuncius within about a year of first observations — a documented, fast turnaround.

provenance.notes: First-batch diversity pick: early_modern, southern_europe (underrepresented region in the current roster), astronomy/physics domain, extremely rich documented evidence including a genuine institutional-conflict/risk narrative distinct from Newton's.
